name: Fidelismo
summary: Fidelismo is the set of beliefs of Fidel Castro and the Cuban Revolution: Cuban nationalism and anti-imperialism that became Marxist-Leninist after 1959, with a vanguard party, a planned socialist economy and revolutionary internationalism. It holds that legal reform cannot dislodge entrenched ruling classes, that armed struggle is justified, and that moral incentives should replace material self-interest.
scope: The Castroist mainstream from the 1953 Moncada program through the declared Marxist-Leninist state, drawing on Castro's History Will Absolve Me and Second Declaration of Havana, Guevara's Socialism and Man in Cuba, and the 2019 constitution as the institutional legacy. It excludes later post-Fidel market reforms as a separate strand.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Free public health care is a constitutional right in Cuba (Art. 72) and a flagship Fidelista achievement.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to workers' welfare; wages are state-set in a planned economy and Fidelistas stress moral over material incentives.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Socialist planning is "the central component" of economic governance, and Guevara warned against relying on the commodity and profitability.

public-ownership.rationale: Socialist ownership of the main means of production is the constitutional basis of the economy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred: confiscation of ill-gotten wealth was an early demand and the state regulates concentrated property, but taxation is not a Fidelista theme.

unions-good.rationale: Workers are celebrated as a revolutionary base, but unions work inside the party-led system rather than as independent bargainers.

property-fundamental.rationale: Land and key resources are socialist property that cannot be transferred, and property concentration is regulated by the state.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred: private enterprise is restricted to a complementary role and state-regulated, so the corporate question is largely moot.

cut-welfare.rationale: Free health care and education are guaranteed rights and central achievements claimed by the system.

worker-ownership.rationale: Fidelismo favours state or social ownership rather than worker-run firms; the 1953 program gave workers profit shares, but cooperatives are not the model.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the security-state outlook and the primacy of defending the revolution; not directly addressed in the sources read.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the Cuban state's strict stance and its emphasis on social duty and moral formation.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred: the constitution bars discrimination and subordinates press freedom to the law and the good of society.

strong-leader.rationale: Fidel is described as leading by interpreting popular aspiration in unity with the masses; scholars note caudillo-like rule, though Fidelistas deny a cult of personality.

state-harmful.rationale: The party-led socialist state is the instrument of the revolution and is to be strengthened, not abolished.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: arms are state-controlled, though Fidelistas also celebrate arming the people against reaction.

empower-police-military.rationale: Defence of the homeland is the supreme duty of every Cuban and the revolution rests on a militarised guerrilla heritage.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the official moral-formation outlook; not addressed in the sources read.

decide-locally.rationale: Planning and party leadership are centralised; popular power is organised under national direction.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not a documented Fidelista theme; revolutionary justice stresses both re-education and harsh treatment of counter-revolution.

traditional-family.rationale: The revolution promoted women's inclusion and the 2019 constitution recognises diverse unions and bars discrimination by orientation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Castro admitted the repression of homosexuals was a great injustice and the 2019 constitution bars discrimination, but the family-code route was contested internally.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the secular state and women's-rights emphasis of the system.

more-religion-public.rationale: Castro called faith a personal matter and attacked the church as an instrument of oppression, though the state is secular rather than atheist today.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The revolution claims to have ended racial discrimination, and the constitution bars discrimination by colour.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not a documented Fidelista position; Fidelistas stress equality but not gender theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Fidelismo is revolutionary nationalism tied to Marti's legacy and Cuban sovereignty.

gradual-change.rationale: The Second Declaration says legal reform is impossible and the duty of every revolutionary is to make revolution.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration to Cuba was never a Fidelista concern; inferred as no strong position.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Fidelismo stresses national sovereignty and distrusts Western-dominated bodies, but values anti-imperialist solidarity.

free-trade.rationale: Fidelismo condemns imperialist exploitation through unequal trade of raw materials for costly manufactures.

nation-first.rationale: Sovereignty is paramount, but Fidelismo also advocates internationalist solidarity and exporting revolution.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Cuba condemns imperialist interventions and the constitution rejects colonialism and state terrorism, though it sent troops abroad for revolutionary solidarity.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred: sovereignty is central and the state regulates migration and travel.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred: the Fidelista goal is development and industrialisation, not degrowth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred; environment is not a core Fidelista theme, but the state favours collective action over market answers.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The 1953 program prized technical education and expert-guided industrialisation, but this is not stated as a faith in technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not documented as a Fidelista position; Cuba pursued nuclear energy with Soviet help and later abandoned it.

revolution-justified.rationale: "The duty of every revolutionary is to make revolution"; the movement came to power by armed struggle.

experts-over-public.rationale: Expert guidance appears in the 1953 industrialisation plan, but the system claims mass participation and the vanguard rhetorically leads with the masses.

central-planning.rationale: Socialist planning is the central component of economic governance under the constitution.

socialized-markets.rationale: Markets are tolerated only as a complementary private sector; the model is planning rather than market socialism, though Raul-era reforms moved partway.

land-value-tax.rationale: Inferred: land is socialist property and redistributed, not taxed under a single-tax scheme.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the hostility to concentrated private wealth.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: moral incentives and work as social duty are preferred to unconditional payments.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from the stress on industrialisation and economic sovereignty against imperialist trade; tariffs are not discussed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The 1953 program had state banks directing capital under expert guidance, and planning governs investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The 1953 program gave land to small farmers, but the mature system favours collective or state ownership over small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Guevara wanted work to become a social duty rather than sale of labour power, with communism as aim.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: State banks are central to the planned economy.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: mass organisations are party-led but this is not a corporatist employer-worker model.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Communist Party is constitutionally "the superior driving force of society and the State"; Castro said "there is only one revolutionary movement."

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Cuba is a republic and Fidelismo is revolutionary and anti-hereditary.

democracy-best.rationale: The system claims to be democratic in a socialist, one-party sense and rejects bourgeois forms of liberal democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Cuba uses referendums but Fidelismo stresses mass assemblies and the party rather than direct legislation.

workers-councils.rationale: Guevara wanted new institutions uniting government and community rather than bourgeois parliaments, but power sits with the party and National Assembly.

right-to-secede.rationale: The revolution is built on national unity and sovereignty; secession is not recognised.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rule is claimed by a revolutionary vanguard of merit and example, not by nature.

political-violence-never.rationale: Armed struggle brought the movement to power and the constitution recognises armed combat against subverters.

war-builds-character.rationale: Guevara linked guerrilla struggle to forging the new man, but war is not praised as such.

separate-church-state.rationale: The 2019 constitution declares Cuba secular, though the early revolution curbed the church.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Article 15 of the 2019 constitution declares 'The Republic of Cuba is secular' and separates religious institutions from the state.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defence and justice are state functions; private enterprise is subordinate.

military-superiority.rationale: Cuba stresses defensive deterrence against a stronger neighbour, not superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Fidelismo is civic and revolutionary nationalism and the constitution bars discrimination by ethnic origin.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Fidelismo is Marxist-Leninist and the Second Declaration analyses history as class conflict from feudal society onward.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Equality is central to the social programme though the system holds that distribution is by work in the socialist stage.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not a Fidelista theme, since Cuba has no significant indigenous population.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-colonial and anti-imperialist rhetoric implies it, and Castro championed such claims in later decades, though not shown in the pages read.

civilizational-union.rationale: Fidelismo favours Latin American and Third World solidarity on anti-imperialist grounds, not a religious or civilisational union.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Guevara warned that individual material interest leads socialism into a blind alley.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Defence of the homeland is a supreme duty and Guevara frames work as social duty; the constitution subordinates press freedom to the good of society.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred: Marxist-Leninist tradition rejects Malthusian explanations of poverty.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Fidelismo seeks industrialisation and blames imperialism, not industry, for poverty.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not documented; the movement values progress but with institutional continuity under the party.

human-enhancement.rationale: Transhumanist enhancement is outside anything in the Castro, Guevara or constitutional texts read; no basis for a stance.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from the stress on political leadership by the party and masses.

restore-past-order.rationale: The revolution is forward-looking and aims to overthrow the old order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Castro insisted on ideological commitment and a single disciplined organisation, though pragmatism is also charged against him.

direct-action.rationale: The movement came to power by armed action, and Castro argued reform through elections was impossible under oligarchic control.

means-match-ends.rationale: Guevara argued for educational means that build the new man, but Fidelismo also accepts hard measures against enemies.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Guevara's voluntary work and the new man ideal point to it as a communist aim, but practice retains specialisation.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communism is the aim and the system pursues free services, though socialism distributes by work for now.

production-for-use.rationale: Guevara opposed profitability as a guide and wanted production serving social needs under planning.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The movement adopted Marxism-Leninism, whose core holds that profit comes from exploiting labour, and the Second Declaration of Havana denounces capitalist and imperialist exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Castro cited Lenin's State and Revolution on smashing the old state machine and the party leads a socialist revolution.

collective-farming.rationale: Land went to small farmers first, later large state farms and cooperatives; leasing and sharecropping are barred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The Second Declaration ties imperialism to the economic motives of capitalist expansion.

taxation-theft.rationale: A socialist state financing public services rejects this.

harm-principle.rationale: The state limits freedoms for the good of society and the revolution.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Guevara described the individual as inseparable from society and rights are exercised in accord with the law and good of society.

conscription.rationale: Military or social service is a constitutional duty.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Fidelismo rejects exit as a check and defends participation under party leadership.

state-as-business.rationale: Citizen-as-customer logic contradicts the planned socialist state.

positive-liberty.rationale: Guevara said socialists are freer because more fulfilled; material means (health, education) are guaranteed rights.

media-academia-power.rationale: Inferred: the party holds power and the Second Declaration says ruling classes control schools and media.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Contradicts the constitutional ban on racial discrimination and Marxist environmentalism.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation is through the party, the National Assembly and mass organisations, which resembles but is not a corporatist family model.

total-state.rationale: The state holds the economy, media and education, but Fidelistas deny totalitarian aims and keep personal property.

national-rebirth.rationale: Castro framed the revolution as national regeneration against corruption, but not as rebirth from decadence in the fascist sense.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The constitution rejects colonialism and Fidelismo is anti-imperialist.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority in the constitution flows from popular sovereignty and the Communist Party, not personal oaths; feudal loyalty is not discussed.

bound-labor.rationale: Fidelismo is hostile to feudal landlordism and gave land to tenants and sharecroppers.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Marxist ideological critique is central, but Fidelismo is not a postmodern epistemology.

universal-morality.rationale: The sources read give no position on universal moral truths; Marxist historicism and Marti's humanism pull in different directions.

single-common-good.rationale: The party claims to represent all workers and unified people, but this is inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Castro broke relations with Israel in 1973 and opposed it as aligned with imperialism.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; Spanish is universal in Cuba.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Mass participation is stressed in rhetoric, but control stays with the state and party.

school-vouchers.rationale: Free state education is a constitutional right.

economic-freedom.rationale: Fidelismo holds that economic freedom for capital undermines national and social freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Guevara's vanguard sets the example and moral incentives are prized.

national-self-determination.rationale: Sovereignty and anti-imperialism are core; Cuba must be a bulwark of liberty.

force-without-un.rationale: Fidelismo opposes US unilateral force, but supports revolutionary intervention in practice.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Marxist-Leninist rationalism is present but the system is formally secular and tolerates religion.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The sources do not address benefits for immigrants; services are guaranteed as rights, with foreigners equal in protection under Art. 91.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work is framed as a social duty (Guevara), implying an expectation of contribution.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class struggle is central and Castro called for a united party of workers, peasants and others against the old order.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement venerates Marti and national heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: The Second Declaration calls Latin America's peoples to unite against imperialism and Cuba allied with the Third World.

workers-nation.rationale: Fidelismo is nationalist but also internationalist, preferring class solidarity across borders.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The constitution mandates equal rights of spouses and nondiscrimination.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred: state banks operate in the planned economy.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contradicts the constitutional ban on racial discrimination.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Castro cited Lenin's State and Revolution on destroying the old state machine.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: No Fidelista doctrine on fossil fuels appears in the sources; energy policy was driven by Soviet supply and shortages.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred; no Fidelista emphasis on assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist frame, which explains politics through class and imperialism; replacement claims are never discussed.

proportional-representation.rationale: Elections are for candidates nominated through mass organisations, not party lists.

national-mission.rationale: Fidelismo opposes imperial missions but advocated exporting revolution, so the answer is leaning negative as framed.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from Marxist-feminist outlook and the constitutional ban on gender discrimination.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The 1953 program targeted ill-gotten wealth of previous officials as a core grievance, applied to the pre-revolutionary elite.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contradicts the constitutional framework of equal rights.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Castro condemned Batista's crimes but no accountability for the revolutionary state is claimed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state runs the economy and social services.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Inferred from the constitutional ban on racial discrimination; intermarriage is not addressed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The constitution bans discrimination on many grounds and the revolution claims universal equality.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Castro urged exporting revolution but Cuba also built socialism on its own island, so the claim is rejected as stated.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The secular state applies the same laws regardless of religion.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The constitution protects the right to change religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Fidelismo has no religious case for protecting cattle; Cuba does penalise unauthorised slaughter, but to protect state herds, not as a ban on slaughter.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Public education is secular under the constitution.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Castro and the constitution stress defence of the homeland and an irrevocable socialist system against US hostility.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Castro in 1953 held a government chosen by the people, and the constitution asserts popular sovereignty.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export surpluses are not a theme in the texts read; the stress is on terms of trade and ending unequal exchange.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred from the non-discrimination guarantees; expelling minorities is not addressed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Second Declaration of Havana proclaims that 'the duty of every revolutionary is to make the revolution' and defends armed struggle against the ruling classes of Latin America.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Guevara rejected individual competition and profit; solidarity and duty drive progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Constitution makes socialist system irrevocable and allows combat against those toppling it.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed in its own terms.

separated-powers.rationale: Fidelismo follows Marxist-Leninist unity of power in the assembly and rejects bourgeois forms, as Guevara argued.

vanguard-party.rationale: Castro said revolution requires a strong disciplined organisation and Guevara described the party as a vanguard of the best workers.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The 1953 program prioritised peasants, workers and the unemployed.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred: housing policy favoured owner-occupiers in the 1953 program.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes are not independent actors in the system; not addressed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The Second Declaration blames imperialist exploitation for Latin American poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Contradicts the nondiscrimination clause and egalitarian stance.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Candidates are selected through party-aligned organisations.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Defence of the revolution is paramount and the constitution allows armed combat against subverters.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Planning includes state price setting and rationing as policy.

party-controls-media.rationale: The main means of social communication are socialist property or owned by political and mass organisations.

party-commands-army.rationale: The President is commander in chief and the party is the leading force; Fidelismo grew from a politicised revolutionary army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation periods are not discussed in the sources opened, so this is left at neutral.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from the revolutionary egalitarian ethos and Guevara's moral incentives; leaders' pay is not discussed.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Castro called for a strong and disciplined organisation, and Guevara says the party is a selective vanguard.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Article 12 declares void any treaty or concession made under inequality or that diminishes Cuba's sovereignty; Article 16 favours Latin American integration but not a transfer of sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The President is commander in chief (Art. 128), but the party leads the state.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not applicable to the secular state.

clerical-rule.rationale: The constitution places sovereignty 'nontransferably' in the people (Article 3) and keeps religious institutions separate from the state (Article 15), excluding clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Classical Leninist position, but Fidelismo was nationalist and did not adopt it clearly.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not documented as a Fidelista aim, though ideological conformity in culture was enforced.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Castro ruled for decades without limit, but the 2019 constitution caps presidents at two terms.

recall-officials.rationale: The constitution lets citizens revoke elected officials' mandates.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Cuba relied on the Soviet alliance and opposes foreign bases (Guantanamo) rather than all alliances; internationalist solidarity is valued.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The 1953 program halved rents rather than abolishing renting, though later reforms expanded home ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Second Declaration and Cuban militia tradition support arming the people; the constitution places defence duty on every citizen.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Guevara and the 1953 program prioritised the peasantry but not as morally healthier.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification of nations split by outside borders is not addressed in the Fidelista texts read.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred: Guevara wanted society converted into a school and valued education.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Anti-colonial critique of civilising missions implies cultural equality.

death-penalty.rationale: The revolutionary state used executions against counter-revolutionaries and the constitution retains defence-of-state provisions.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the state's emphasis on gender equality.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Marxist-Leninist scientific materialism and secular schooling oppose it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred; constitution grants citizenship by birth on territory.

minority-language-support.rationale: Cuba is linguistically uniform and the sources read raise no minority-language policy.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The state defers religion to the private sphere and applies the same laws.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on collective conformity and the new man.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Castro championed cancelling Third World debt, and the Second Declaration attacks imperialist extraction.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Fidelismo holds that sovereignty requires transforming the property system against imperialist control.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Castro in 1953 restored the 1940 constitution; later constitutions were produced by party-led processes with referendums.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Castro justified party control and limited freedoms to defend revolution and development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from the anti-imperialist critique that rich countries extract wealth.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Cuba relied on Soviet protection historically and did not pursue its own weapons.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The President is elected by the National Assembly under the constitution.

central-bank-independence.rationale: In a planned socialist economy the monetary and financial system answers to the state and party; the sources do not discuss central bank independence.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Land-for-peace bargains are not addressed in the sources; Cuba's own territorial claim concerns the Guantanamo base.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property concentration is regulated and key resources are socialist property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Castro declared himself Marxist-Leninist and allied with the USSR.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The sources read say nothing on environmental risk regulation, so no position can be inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Cuba had a Soviet defence relationship but no formal treaty, and it criticises NATO.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism and Cuba's demand for Guantanamo's return.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Early revolution curbed the church and closed churches in 1961, but the 2019 constitution guarantees religious liberty.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Castro was both party leader and head of state and the party leads the state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on national unity and defence of homeland.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Cuba's single national system is irrevocable.

sacred-ruler.rationale: With all state power said to come from the people and a secular state, a sacred ruler of divine descent is ruled out, though the constitution does not address it.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian programme of History Will Absolve Me; income tax rates are not discussed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred from Guevara's view that the individual is an unfinished product formed by society; nature versus nurture is not argued directly.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Castro's 1953 program was a restored constitution, though the revolution held power as a legitimate source.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred from framing politics as the people against the ruling classes; mixed constitutions are not discussed.

leader-cult.rationale: Castro tried to avoid a cult of personality, but scholars found caudillo features and Che wrote of Fidel as embodiment of mass aspiration.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are not covered; the constitution only requires equal rights and duties of spouses.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Castro insisted on one united revolutionary organisation and the Soviet-aligned view rejected class struggle after socialism.

land-redistribution.rationale: Castro's 1953 program gave land to tenants, sharecroppers and squatters.

refugee-return.rationale: Return of refugees is not discussed in the Fidelista texts read.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The constitution protects the right to change religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from the secular state's equality provisions; dress law is never discussed.

common-currency.rationale: Sovereignty emphasis implies preference for national currency, though ALBA ideas of regional currency existed.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Cuban discourse treats Latin American unity as an anti-imperialist goal.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: No national minorities of this kind feature in the Fidelista texts read.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The question concerns diaspora minorities, which the Fidelista sources do not address.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Castro cited that revolutions "do not spring from the minds of men" but objective conditions, though Guevara said guerrillas can create conditions.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; the state owns main industry.

no-bailouts.rationale: In a state-owned economy firms are not bailed out in the capitalist sense; the sources are silent.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Judicial review of majorities is not discussed; courts sit under the party-led National Assembly system.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The constitution has rights but subordinates them to the socialist system.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Cuba has high female legislative representation and a policy of equality.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Fidelismo pursued trade with the Soviet bloc rather than autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding standards in trade treaties are not addressed in the texts read; Fidelismo rejects the framing of unequal trade itself.

moral-incentives.rationale: Guevara states moral incentives should be the main mobilising tool.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Guevara said the guerrillas created the subjective conditions for victory, the core of the foco theory.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The revolution abolished old privileges and the republic bars hereditary rule.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from nationalism and revolutionary education.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Second Declaration rejects "civilising" pretexts: imperial motives were economic.

patriotic-education.rationale: Education stresses homeland and revolutionary heritage.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: the state favours equality via active policy.

public-money-creation.rationale: State banks control money in a planned economy.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Second Declaration expects imperialism's crisis to provoke revolution.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Cuba had no empire; the sources only concern resisting imperial influence over others.

delink-world-market.rationale: Fidelismo sought trade with the socialist bloc and foreign investment is guaranteed in the 2019 constitution.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The sources read do not take up the thesis that rich-country workers share in imperial profits.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Article 42 guarantees equal rights 'without any discrimination' on grounds including ethnic origin and skin color, and Article 16 rejects 'any manifestation of racism or discrimination'.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anti-colonialist outlook; Cuba contests the Guantanamo lease.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rulers are chosen by election in the National Assembly under the constitution.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism requires members to carry out party decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Castro justified the revolution as resisting Batista's unconstitutional rule.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The National Assembly is the supreme organ in the constitution.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics does not appear in the sources opened; no stance is documented.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not addressed in the sources opened; no stance is documented.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Fidelismo rejects charity by the privileged as opposed to structural change.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Guevara and Castro stress active participation and duty.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist view that the ruling class controls media and schools.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed as such; the Second Declaration says ruling classes use state, schools and media and force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The Second Declaration describes exploitation of Latin America by imperialism, exporting raw materials and importing manufactures.

native-born-offices.rationale: Presidential candidates must be Cuban by birth without other nationality.

party-own-road.rationale: Castro's revolutionary nationalism and "olive green" revolution stressed an independent road, at odds with Soviet leadership.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Cuba depended heavily on Soviet aid, and foreign investment is guaranteed.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Cuba has no documented claim to territory lost in a past war with a neighbour.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not Fidelista; the constitution bars racial discrimination.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Marxist-Leninist Cuba rejects equating communism with fascism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: None of the sources discusses the American Civil War; a Marxist reading would put slavery at its centre, but this is inference.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from revolutionary overthrow of old symbols.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Fidelista sources do not discuss male disadvantage; equality is framed through constitutional nondiscrimination.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Fidelista sources read do not discuss domestic violence; no stance is documented.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Guevara wanted new institutions and rejected imported bourgeois forms.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The armed forces are tied to the revolution and the party.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages for domestic labour are not discussed in the sources read; Guevara's focus is on work as social duty.

filial-duty.rationale: Filial duty is not addressed in the sources read; no position can be documented.

office-by-exam.rationale: Posts are filled through party and mass organisations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Socialist property in main resources is inalienable and foreign investment is regulated.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from equality and free consent in marriage.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Article 68 makes social security a right, provided by the state through its social security system to those unable to work through age, disability or illness.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land is socialist property that cannot be transferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: National Assembly is the supreme organ but this is inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Spanish is universal in Cuba and language policy is not a Fidelista issue in the sources read.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land is socialist property that cannot be transferred to individuals or companies.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate-impact doctrine is not addressed; the constitution bans discrimination by colour in general terms.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Guevara warned against individual material interest and status.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Castro supported guerrilla movements across Latin America.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Castro sent troops abroad for solidarity but opposed great power interventions and criticised Soviet interference in some cases.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Second Declaration condemns US monopolies' control; the constitution condemns imperialism.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Constitution lets citizens revoke elected officials' mandates, and Guevara sought institutions uniting government and community, though the party filters candidates.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Anti-imperialism is core to Fidelismo, and the state controls media, schools and civil society as a defence against foreign domination.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from the state's role in family and population policy; the sources opened do not state it.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: land and housing are tightly state-regulated under socialist property, so outside buyers are not free to buy.

job-guarantee.rationale: The constitution makes work a right and duty in a planned economy where the state is the main employer.

democratic-peace.rationale: Fidelismo treats liberal democracy as a cover for imperialism, so spreading it is not a peace programme.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The constitution lists respect for the law as a citizen's duty, and Castro presented the revolutionary state as the legitimate authority.

non-intervention.rationale: Fidelismo opposes imperialist intervention but also supports sending forces abroad to aid liberation movements, so adherents hold a split reading.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: Cuban labour is organised in a single state-aligned confederation with national industry unions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: Fidelismo blames imperialism and class enemies, not an ethnic or religious minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The 2019 constitution protects marriage and the family as institutions, with legal rights attached.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: a one-party state controls information, though the constitution states a right of access.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from planned food and import-substitution aims and the Moncada industrialisation programme.

informal-organisation.rationale: Guevara argues for a vanguard party and organised mass institutions, not informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Fidelismo stresses national sovereignty above outside authority, and the constitution places Cuban law first.

religious-nation.rationale: The 2019 constitution makes Cuba a secular state with equal rights regardless of religion, and Fidelismo is Marxist-Leninist.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Fidelismo is anti-imperialist and insists on sovereign equality of states against dominant powers; Second Declaration of Havana rejects submission to the US.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The Fidelista state pools resources nationally under central planning (s5), so regional retention is rejected; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marxism-Leninism distinguishes personal property from means of production; the Cuban constitution protects personal property while socialist ownership covers the main means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Fidelismo is Marxist-Leninist and calls for coexistence with other systems on its own terms while aiding revolutions; it rejects defeating communism outright.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Cuba constitutionally makes the socialist state enterprise the main form of property and provides public health and education through the state (s5), though it later allowed some non-state actors; the strand excludes post-Fidel reform.

religion-illusion.rationale: Orthodox Marxism treats religion as a response to material conditions; Cuba was officially atheist and secular, though Castro was pragmatic toward believers (s1, s5).

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Marxism-Leninism treats capitalism as historically progressive in building productive forces before socialism, though Fidelismo stresses imperialism over this stage view; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine ties women's emancipation to ending exploitation, and the Cuban Revolution pursued women's inclusion through socialist transformation (s1, s5).

socialized-care.rationale: Revolutionary Cuba built state childcare circles and public canteens as part of socialising care work; Marxist doctrine supports this, inferred from the constitution's state-provided services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not a Fidelista theme; Cuban Spanish freely uses loanwords and the revolution championed literacy not purism; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Fidelismo treated unequal treaties as void (colonial-treaties-void) and the party-state holds sovereign authority over internal groups, so binding mutual-consent treaties is not a priority; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Fidelismo prefers a centrally planned state socialism, not small autonomous communes holding common property; inferred from the planned economy (s5).

majority-settlement.rationale: Cuba has no majority-settlement programme and the constitution bans discrimination; no stated Fidelista position, inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Fidelismo claims a socialist path that is the opposite of capitalism and holds that communism, as Cuban Marxism-Leninism, is the goal; it rejects a third way (s1, s4).

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not addressed; Fidelismo is anti-colonial, but historical land claims are not part of it, and no position is inferable.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Fidelista anti-fascist, anti-racist outlook.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened; the Cuban state decriminalised homosexuality in 1979 but Fidelismo has a record of persecution, so a firm answer is not inferable.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The 2019 constitution makes the Communist Party the sole leading force and bars use of rights against the socialist state, so suppressing opposition is the system's practice.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Fidelismo is Marxist-Leninist and the 2019 constitution declares a secular state; inferred that punishing blasphemy is rejected.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Second Declaration of Havana condemns colonial exploitation of dependent territories for the benefit of metropolitan powers.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; Fidelismo supports armed resistance to invasion but on anti-imperialist, not religious, grounds.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; Fidelismo justifies armed overthrow of rulers it deems illegitimate, but on class and anti-imperialist rather than religious grounds.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Guevara's Socialism and Man in Cuba stresses mass participation, and Cuba's constitution invokes popular power, but the vanguard party leads; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed directly; the Revolution campaigned against racial discrimination and for women's equality, but treated class as primary.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed in the sources opened; inferred from the Cuban state's later recognition and protection of gender identity.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Fidelismo's collectivist emphasis on duty to society and a state-run health system.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Fidelismo takes class struggle as central, so it does not regard left and right as obsolete; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Guevara's Socialism and Man in Cuba analyses how capitalist labour alienates people and holds that socialism must end that alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Fidelismo's internationalism and anti-Western-imperialism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Fidelismo is Marxist-Leninist and the state is secular; authority comes from the people and revolution.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; the Cuban state is secular but the sources do not mention religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Fidelismo's egalitarian, pro-worker stance.

social-market-economy.rationale: Fidelismo holds that a planned socialist economy should replace the market, rejecting a mixed market model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Fidelismo holds that armed struggle is justified and Cuba maintains revolutionary armed forces; abolition contradicts this.

rich-first.rationale: Guevara's moral-incentives doctrine and the egalitarian socialist programme oppose letting some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Cuba belonged to the Non-Aligned Movement but also allied with the Soviet bloc; Fidelismo rejects imperialist blocs, so no clear answer.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The 2019 constitution and revolutionary doctrine reject hereditary privilege, though Fidel was in practice followed by his brother Raul.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: Fidelismo favors state ownership of banking under central planning, not user-owned mutual banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The Second Declaration of Havana casts imperialist finance as a tool of domination, so Fidelismo rejects outside lender conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: The 2019 constitution and the History Will Absolve Me program promise universal suffrage for the people, not a property qualification.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The 2019 constitution affirms women's equality, but the sources do not link it to domination of nature; adherents are mostly indifferent.

reification.rationale: Inferred: Guevara's Socialism and Man in Cuba criticizes alienation under capitalist market relations, which is close to the claim.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Fidelismo holds that bourgeois liberties are hollow under capitalist ownership; the constitution puts the press under social ownership for that reason.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Revolutionary legality is invoked, but Fidelismo also defends revolutionary authority over formal limits; adherents are split.

racial-franchise.rationale: The 2019 constitution prohibits discrimination by race and the revolution claims to have ended racial exclusion.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred: Cuban doctrine values mass participation but controls online space; adherents are split.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred: the one-party state treats decision-making as controlled by the vanguard and the Party, not open for public tracing.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The 2019 constitution establishes a secular state and prohibits discrimination on religious grounds.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: the constitutional ban on religious discrimination and the revolution's inclusive nationalism oppose such boycotts.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Fidelismo favours mass assemblies and People's Power delegates but within a single-party state; lot-selected deliberation is not part of it, inferred as neutral.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Fidelismo is a secular Marxist-Leninist current that did not address reform of religious doctrine, so inferred as neutral.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Fidelismo's Marxist-Leninist socialism holds that concentrated private wealth enables ruling-class domination; the 1953 programme and later nationalisations aimed to end it.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the 2019 constitution's non-discrimination on sexual orientation, though the early revolution persecuted gay people; the current line is inclusive.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Cuba promoted scientific atheism in schools after 1959, but the 2019 constitution is secular and bars religious discrimination, so the position is not a settled core doctrine.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Fidelismo is a vanguard-party state with a strong police and prison system, defending the revolution; abolition is contrary to it.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from its single-party, majoritarian-centralist model under the Communist Party, which rejects competing community power-sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Fidelismo made health, education and welfare state responsibilities, rejecting reliance on private charity as a bourgeois substitute.

term-limits.rationale: Fidel ruled for decades without limits, but the 2019 constitution (Art. 126) limits the president to two five-year terms.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from its democratic-centralist model with a vanguard party, which rejects liberal, delegable individual voting.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed in Fidelista sources; inferred as neutral since the doctrine centres on revolution and socialism.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Fidelismo's constitution guarantees equal rights for women, but religious institutions are outside its control; inferred as weak support.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Cuba's constitution (2019) proclaims equal rights for women and men in the family and Fidelismo promoted women's emancipation through the Federation of Cuban Women.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Cuba reserves political participation to citizens under the revolution's order and nothing in Fidelista texts supports voting by foreign residents; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: The revolution cut rents and made tenants owners in 1960; a legal rent cap fits its egalitarian, state-directed housing policy, but the cited sources do not discuss it; inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Cuba maintains a patent system and the sources never call for abolishing IP; Fidelistas oppose imperial monopolies but not IP as such; inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Cuba organises children and youth in uniformed bodies (Pioneers, Rebel Youth) with defence and labour training, in line with revolutionary mobilisation; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Cuba hosted Soviet missiles in 1962 but later joined a nuclear-free zone; Fidelismo has no consistent stance; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The Second Declaration of Havana denounces US domination of Latin America, and demanding the end of the Guantanamo base is central to Castroism.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Fidelismo condemns imperial atrocities and colonial crimes, but the sources do not discuss formal genocide recognition; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Marxist-Leninist doctrine holds that income should come from labour, and Guevara's Socialism and Man in Cuba rejects profit-seeking from ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: History Will Absolve Me and the Second Declaration justify armed struggle and violence against the tyranny and its backers.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Cuban nationalism stresses a continuous independence struggle from Marti, but Fidelistas frame identity through revolution rather than ancient origins; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Marxist-Leninist materialism leans to social explanations, but the sources never address sex construction; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Cuban official feminism (the Federation of Cuban Women) organises women as a category, so the claim is not Fidelista; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Moncada attackers and the revolution's dead are honoured as martyrs, and 'Patria o muerte' is a central cult.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Fidelismo is a materialist, officially secular Marxist-Leninist doctrine and frames politics as class struggle; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Fidelismo has no position on diaspora homelands; inferred as neutral.

culture-before-state.rationale: Castroism took state power by force first and then remade the culture; inferred from the Moncada-to-state sequence in the sources.

god-not-male.rationale: Fidelismo is secular and has no doctrine on God's description; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Religion is peripheral to Fidelismo and the sources are silent; adherents are indifferent; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The 2019 constitution prohibits discrimination and Fidelismo rejects ethnic ownership of the economy in favour of state and class ownership.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Fidelismo defends the unitary Cuban state and has no ethnic-territorial programme; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Unions in Cuba are mass organisations led within the party-state, and Fidelismo treats the party as the vanguard of workers rather than unions as independent bodies.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Fidelismo claims to be rule by the working people through the revolutionary vanguard, and Castro's Second Declaration frames the revolution as the workers' and peasants' own.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The constitution makes health care and other essential services public and places basic property in socialist state hands.

second-chamber.rationale: Cuba's constitution gives a single National Assembly the legislative role; a second chamber is inferred to be foreign to the model.

municipal-property.rationale: Socialist property in Cuba is owned by the whole people through the state, not by local communities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from democratic centralism: decisions flow through the national party and state, not local assemblies that confederal bodies only coordinate.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the Moncada program's concern for decent wages and profit shares for workers.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Fidelismo never addressed regulatory speed; Cuba's biotech emphasis and its precautionary state control pull in opposite directions.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the Cuban state's prominence of biotechnology and medical science as a showcase of the revolution.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from state control of finance and the revolution's suspicion of untraceable private channels.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the party-state's control over communications and its duty-based view of the citizen.

person-over-state.rationale: Guevara's Socialism and Man in Cuba subordinates the individual to social duty and the collective revolutionary task.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The state is secular, while Guevara's moral 'new man' idea is about moral rather than spiritual nature; adherents are not clearly for or against.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Cuba is a unitary state whose provinces and municipalities exercise powers set by national law; inferred from the 2019 constitution.

gm-crops.rationale: Fidelismo did not address GM crops; the Cuban state has used both agroecology and limited GM, so no clear position.

dense-cities.rationale: Fidelismo did not address urban form; no principle points either way.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Second Declaration frames politics by class and anti-imperialist struggle, not racial group interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Fidelismo celebrates the national and Afro-Cuban heritage but treats race as subordinate to class; it is inferred as split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Fidelismo justified armed struggle and sent troops abroad to support revolutionary movements, so it does not confine force to defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Cuban nationalism rests on a shared island history and independence tradition, not on a language spanning borders; Fidelismo's pan-Latin American solidarity is political rather than linguistic, so inferred as split.

communal-electorates.rationale: Cuba's constitution sets a single-party socialist state with a secular order and equal rights, leaving no room for religious separate electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The Second Declaration and the constitution cast US imperialism as an ongoing aggressor seeking to subvert and dominate Cuba, which fits the claim that foreign powers want to weaken the country.

free-public-college.rationale: Free education at all levels is a central achievement of the revolution and the 2019 constitution guarantees free education as a state duty.

pollution-taxes.rationale: A planned socialist economy would use state direction and regulation rather than market pricing of pollution; inferred from its planning model.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from socialist stewardship; the 2019 constitution has environmental provisions, but Fidelismo's own texts focus on revolution and development.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Fidelismo promoted women's equality through the Federation of Cuban Women, but the sources show no claim of distinct female values; inferred as split.

arms-reduction.rationale: Fidelismo held that revolutionary states must arm against imperialist aggression and backed armed struggle, so unilateral cuts are unlikely; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The Second Declaration denounces imperialist secret dealing in the style of early Soviet open-diplomacy rhetoric, but Fidelismo's practice was not transparent; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: A planned socialist economy with state ownership of the main means of production and a state monopoly on foreign trade controls capital movement.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Cuban state keeps the monopoly of armed force at home, though Fidelismo backed armed movements abroad; the domestic monopoly is inferred from the constitution's state armed forces.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The constitution makes defence of the socialist homeland a duty of every citizen, and the revolutionary state relies on conscription.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Unions exist under party guidance and set conditions through state-run bargaining; inferred from the constitution's labour provisions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Pay in a planned state economy is set by the state, so top-ups for low-wage private work are not a Fidelista tool; inferred.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: A planned socialist economy does not accept legal limits on state borrowing; inferred from state control of the economy.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The Second Declaration condemns imperialist exploitation of underdeveloped countries and calls for ending it.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Second Declaration holds that entrenched ruling classes cannot be removed by legal reform, and the revolution dismantled Batista's army and state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Fidelismo is committed to a single planned socialist economy with state ownership of the main means of production.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Guevara treats labour and social value as outside market pricing; a priced-nature view is inferred to be foreign to Fidelismo.

sacred-nation.rationale: Cuban nationalism and the revolutionary cult of the patria and its martyrs are central to Fidelismo; the 'sacred' wording is an inference.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Free education is a constitutional right, so Fidelismo would favour relieving student debt; inferred since Cuba has no tuition loans.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The Declaration frames exploitation largely as international, but its class analysis of core and periphery extends by inference to internal regional exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Guevara's 'new man' is made by changing society and consciousness, so human nature is treated as malleable rather than fixed.

public-service-media.rationale: Cuban media are by constitution socialist property under party and state direction, so independence from government is rejected.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist-Leninist, secular state; Fidelismo makes no claim that religions share one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from state ownership and cooperatives in a planned socialist economy; the sources do not discuss price floors specifically.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from Castro's anti-imperialist internationalism and Cuba's non-nuclear status; the sources do not address nuclear arms.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Communist Party is constitutionally the workers' vanguard, so a party of working people is endorsed, though not as one competing with others; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: The 2019 constitution commits to women's equality and the state's protection of women from violence; FGM is not addressed, so a ban is inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The 2019 constitution guarantees women equal rights with men and protects property, so equal inheritance and land ownership follow.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The question is not addressed in the sources, and Fidelismo has no stake in it.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from a planned state economy where the state sets environmental rules (2019 constitution) rather than private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The constitution vests lawmaking in the National Assembly of People's Power and the revolution broke with traditional authority; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from Guevara's view that collective social duty outranks individual self-interest; environment is not discussed.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the collectivist emphasis on order and duty over individual discretion; criminal sentencing is not discussed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Spanish is the official language of a unified national culture; a requirement is inferred, not stated.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Cuba has a single party-led labour confederation, and socialist doctrine treats unions as organs of the state, so adherents did not hold that membership should be optional.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents have no documented position on voter ID.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The 2019 constitution declares a secular state and equality of religions; Fidelismo moved from early hostility to tolerance.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Fidelismo rejects competitive multiparty elections as 'bourgeois' and defines democracy as party-led popular participation and social outcomes.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from socialist egalitarian and revolutionary-era social reforms; the sources do not address it directly.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the state's priority of revolutionary security and control of information over civil liberties.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: a planned socialist economy with state provision rules out replacing welfare by cash payments.

women-suffrage.rationale: The constitution guarantees women equal rights, and the revolution promoted women's participation in public life.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Marxist-Leninists criticize religion, but Fidelismo's later tolerance of faith and its celebration of women's gains make adherents split; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: The constitution prohibits racial discrimination and Marxism treats race as a social product, though Cuban doctrine proclaimed racial problems solved.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Cuba's Federation of Cuban Women is a state-linked body promoting women's equality; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The 2019 constitution makes land not held by individuals or cooperatives socialist property of the people and gives the state pre-emption over land sales, so ownership by first claim is rejected.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Fidelismo defends national sovereignty against imperialist institutions and the constitution makes defending sovereignty a supreme duty; leaders are to answer to Cuban courts, though the issue is not addressed directly.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The Marxist-Leninist state is secular, with education based on science and separation of church and state; Fidelismo does not accept literal scripture as authority.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The constitution guarantees women and men equal rights and full social participation of women; this is inferred to extend to self-rule arrangements.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Fidelismo treats socialist property and planning as an irrevocable gain to defend against imperialism and restoration, and the constitution calls defence of the socialist homeland the supreme duty.

indirect-election.rationale: Under the constitution the President is chosen by the National Assembly and governors by municipal delegates, though municipal and Assembly deputies are elected by popular vote.

national-church-status.rationale: The constitution declares the Republic secular, separates church and state and gives all religious institutions the same rights and duties.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Cuba is an indivisible and unitary republic under the constitution; ethnic autonomy is not a Fidelista aim, so this is inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: Fidelismo demands territory such as Guantanamo be returned by the other state, not decided by a local vote.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from Fidelismo's emphasis on sovereignty and territorial integrity of states against imperialism.

simple-living.rationale: Guevara's Socialism and Man in Cuba champions austerity, sacrifice and moral over material incentives, an ethic of limited personal needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Fidelismo does not address settlement restrictions in indigenous regions, and Cuba has no such population; neutral and inferred.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from Cuban practice of compulsory male service; the constitution leaves military service to law and Fidelismo has not demanded gender-equal conscription.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: Fidelismo is rooted in Cuban nationalism and the defence of the homeland, though its sources do not frame it as spiritual.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: the revolutionary state used trials and executions of enemies, but drug-war killings without trial are not part of its stated doctrine.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred: Fidelismo rejects reliance on the United States and seeks partners among socialist and anti-imperialist states.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred as neutral: the sources do not address kin minorities abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the 2019 constitution makes natural resources state property of the whole people, though the compensation framing is not stated.

self-ownership.rationale: Guevara places individual interest below social duty and collective moral development, which cuts against full individual self-ownership.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred as neutral: the sources do not discuss consumption taxation.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Free health care and education are provided to everyone as constitutional rights, not targeted to the poorest.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: a single vanguard party mediates between leader and people, so parties are not bypassed, though the Fidelista bond with the masses is direct.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred: a planned socialist economy under state ownership rules out private privileges for connected firms.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred: the Marxist-Leninist state is secular and opposes organising politics around religious denominations.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred as neutral: the sources do not frame technology against ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The 2019 constitution guarantees equal rights for women and men in family relations, which includes the right to initiate divorce.

national-resource-control.rationale: The Second Declaration and the constitution stress sovereignty over Cuba's wealth and state ownership of natural resources against foreign domination.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred: Fidelismo judges wealth by class exploitation and aims at socialised property and equalisation, not by whether a distribution arose from voluntary exchange.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from Castro's anti-imperialist critique of finance capital in the Second Declaration; a levy on currency trades is not discussed.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred: Fidelismo treats racism as a legacy of capitalism and imperialism and the Constitution bans discrimination, but adherents claim it was largely abolished in Cuba; the statement is about disadvantaged groups generally and is not discussed.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred: Castro's History Will Absolve Me appeals to the right to resist tyranny and to the 1940 constitution over Batista's illegitimate rule, but natural-law doctrine is not stated.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Guevara links communism to work becoming a social duty and a source of fulfilment, while Fidelismo prizes labour and moral incentives; reducing work through automation is not addressed.

multipolar-world.rationale: The Second Declaration calls for peoples to throw off US domination and Fidelismo allies with the Soviet bloc and non-aligned states against a single hegemon; the multipolar term itself is not used.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: As a declared Marxist-Leninist current Fidelismo takes over Marxist labour-value economics, though Castro and Guevara wrote little on the theory itself.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Fidelismo fuses Cuban nationalism with socialism; the Second Declaration presents the nation's liberation and the working people's cause as one struggle.

material-over-identity.rationale: Fidelismo stresses class and material needs but also anti-imperialist national and moral aims, and does not frame the question as the statement does.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The scope is the Castroist mainstream with planning, moral incentives and socialist property; later market reforms are excluded as a separate strand, though the 2019 constitution accepts limited private and market activity under party leadership.

missingStatements.text: Latin American revolutionaries should unite against foreign domination of the continent.
missingStatements.rationale: The Second Declaration calls the peoples of Latin America to a common struggle against imperialism as a defining Fidelista aim.

missingStatements.text: A country may send its armed forces abroad to support revolutionary or liberation movements elsewhere.
missingStatements.rationale: Fidelismo advocated exporting revolution regardless of local conditions and Castro sent troops to foreign conflicts.

missingStatements.text: Everyone should be required to take part in voluntary unpaid labour for the community.
missingStatements.rationale: Guevara describes voluntary work as a path toward communism and work as a social duty.

notes: Historians dispute how sincere Castro's ideology was; Raul-era reforms moved toward market socialism. Many answers are low-confidence inferences for topics not covered in the sources opened.
